title: Mean-night warmth gave no clear change in local frog-call richness slopes in four US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether mean survey-night temperature changed the local temperature slope of four-species heard-call richness. We used 104,240 stop visits in 10,424 complete runs in Northeast and Midwest US samples in 2001-2007 and 2008-2015. Models controlled survey run, site by seasonal window, and order by window by year. All four interaction estimates were negative, from -0.047 to -0.006 recorded species per stop per 5 C local contrast per 5 C mean-night rise. All four adjusted route and year intervals included zero. Seasonal slope controls moved estimates toward zero. Planned checks did not establish a common interaction. An independent solver agreed within 9e-11. These overlapping survey records extend a prior average-slope test; they are not independent source validation. Selected mild nights, temperature reading errors, unmeasured local conditions and few years limit inference. The result does not identify true richness or a causal warming effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Local slope changes with mean-night temperature. Main and seasonal-control intervals include zero in all four samples.
